name: cua-driver
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw and other agents, on macOS, Windows and Linux
short: Lets your agent operate real desktop apps on macOS, Windows or Linux, then check that the task actually worked.
what: A skill for the Cua Driver CLI and MCP server. Your agent reads an app's accessibility tree, acts through element tokens, menu paths, window geometry or pixel coordinates, then checks the result from a fresh snapshot. It can also drive browser pages and record runs when you ask.
who: People who want an agent to do GUI tasks in apps that have no API. If the job can be done with code or an API, you don't need this.
needs: A coding agent that can load skills or connect to an MCP server
The system permissions Cua Driver asks for to see and control apps

steps.title: Install Cua Driver on macOS or Linux
Add the skill to your agent
steps.text: The `cua` installer shows a checklist that includes the cua-driver MCP and skill for your agents. Pass `--only cua-driver` to skip the checklist. It then runs `cua auth login`, which offers to install skills into your agents.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Ask it to compute 6 × 7 in Calculator and check that the app shows 42.

watch: Every install command pipes a script from cua.ai straight into your shell. Read the script before you run it.
The agent controls real apps on your machine. Foreground mode can move your cursor and change focus, and the skill says to use it only after you allow visible control.
The `unrestricted` permission profile skips Cua's approval prompts. Stick with `standard` unless you know you want that.
The `cua` installer signs you in with `cua auth login`.
The optional cua-perception extension is not MIT. It includes AGPL-licensed parts.
